c.intro: A short call to understand your business, goals and customers, and to check we are the right team for it.
do: Discovery call about your business, customers and goals
Quick review of your website, social presence and competitors
Recommendation of the services that fit now, and what can wait
get: Call recap with goals and next steps
Proposal with scope, phases and timeline
need: Links to what exists today: website, app, socials, brand files

t.purpose: Qualify the lead, understand the business, and send a proposal they say yes to.
steps: Research the lead before the call: website, socials, Google reviews, 3 competitors
Send the discovery questionnaire 24 hours before the call
Run the call with the question list; record with permission
Log the lead and call notes in Notion → Leads
Send the recap email within 24 hours
Draft the proposal: problem, goals, scope by phase, deliverables, timeline
Walk the client through the proposal on a call, not only by email
On acceptance, duplicate the project template in Notion and book the kickoff
t.exit: Proposal accepted, kickoff booked, project page created in Notion.

c.intro: We study your business, market, competitors and customers so every later decision rests on evidence instead of guesses.
do: Kickoff workshop with you and your team
Business and market research (secondary research)
Customer interviews and surveys (primary research)
Competitor analysis: feature-by-feature comparison, what each competitor does best, and the gap you can own
UX audit of your current website or app, if you have one
Review of your analytics and current numbers
get: UX audit report with prioritised fixes (existing products)
need: Access to analytics, website and social accounts
3 to 5 customers we can talk to
Time from you and key team members for interviews

t.purpose: Understand the business, the market and the users well enough to define the right problem.
steps: Run the kickoff: goals, success metrics, stakeholders, constraints
Duplicate the project template in Notion: User Research gallery with one page per research document, all set to Not started
Collect access: analytics, hosting, domain, socials, ad accounts
Secondary research: market, trends, reviews, forums
Competitor Analysis page: overview, feature matrix, what to borrow, strategies to apply, the gap, top 3 moves
Recruit 5 users; interview with a script; record and transcribe
Send a short survey when the audience is large
UX audit if a product exists: heuristics, accessibility, performance, funnel
Start the Design Inspirations page: Refero and Mobbin references grouped by section
Synthesise interviews in Miro: affinity map → themes → insights
t.exit: Competitor Analysis set to Done in Notion; interview insights synthesised and stored.

c.intro: We turn the research into a clear strategy and scope that you approve before any design starts.
do: User personas: goals, pain points, what makes them buy, and how to attract each one
User flows covering every path, including drop-offs, failures and automations
Attraction strategy: what each page section must do and which channel brings which customer
UX strategy: mobile layout rules, the order of trust signals, and where calls to action go
Sitemap, feature scope and roadmap: what goes into version 1 and what comes later
Strategy brief, and a research presentation that walks you through everything
need: Written approval of strategy and scope

t.purpose: Turn research into personas, flows and rules, agreed in writing before design.
steps: User Personas page: 3 to 4 personas with decision levers and how to attract each
Userflows page: zone-by-zone flow with every decision, failure and automation
Attraction Strategy page: sections × personas × copy direction; channels × personas
UX Strategy page: mobile anatomy, layout rules, trust ladder, CTAs and scroll depth
Sitemap and MVP scope with MoSCoW
Strategy Brief page; PRD.md for every build project
Build the UX Research Presentation from the pages above
Present to the client, record changes, get written sign-off
t.exit: Signed-off brief, sitemap and scope. Anything new after this goes through a change request.

c.intro: We give your business a clear identity and design every screen in Figma, grounded in UX laws, accessibility and your story.
do: Design inspirations: curated references and 2 to 3 directions to choose from
Brand system when needed: logo, colours, typography, visual style, graphic elements, voice, icons, layout and mockups
Wireframes of your key pages, following the UX strategy
High-fidelity UI design in Figma for desktop and mobile
Clickable prototype to try the product before it is built
Design system of reusable components, documented in Storybook
Copywriting that tells your story to your customers
Checks for accessibility (WCAG), UX laws and design psychology
need: Feedback within 2 to 3 working days per round

t.purpose: Design the right solution and hand developers a system, not just screens.
steps: Finish Design Inspirations: references by section; present 2 to 3 directions
Branding page (when in scope): logo system, colour system, typography, visual style, graphic elements, brand voice, iconography, layout design, mockups
Wireframes page: one per key page, in the section order from UX Strategy
Set up Figma variables: colour, type, spacing, radius
High-fidelity UI with auto layout, desktop and mobile
Write the UX copy from the Attraction Strategy copy directions
Check contrast (WCAG AA), tap targets and the UX Strategy layout rules
Prototype the main flows; test with 3 to 5 users when possible
Build components in Storybook from the tokens
Developer handoff: Dev Mode links, DESIGN.md, exported assets
t.exit: Client signs off the designs; DESIGN.md and tokens are ready for build.

c.intro: We engineer the product with the right architecture and stack, clean code, built-in security and a CMS you control.
do: System design and architecture planned for your scale
A tech stack chosen for your needs
Front-end, back-end and database development
Integrations: payments, WhatsApp, email, CRM and AI features
A content management system so you can edit content yourself
Security from day one: logins, roles, data protection
Testing on real devices and browsers
Weekly progress updates with a staging link

t.purpose: Ship clean, documented, secure code that matches the signed-off design.
steps: Write ARCHITECTURE.md: stack, data model, roles, integrations
Create the repo with README, CLAUDE.md and .env.example
Set up local, staging and production environments
Build in weekly sprints; demo on staging every week
Code review on every pull request
Integrate CMS, payments, WhatsApp, email and analytics
Run the security checklist: auth, roles, validation, secrets, rate limits
QA: cross-browser, mobile, accessibility, Lighthouse
Client tests on staging (UAT); fix and re-test
t.exit: UAT passed with no open critical or high-severity bugs.

c.intro: We launch carefully, set up SEO and analytics, and hand everything over in your name.
do: Production deployment with a launch checklist
Domain, SSL and email setup
SEO foundations: page titles, meta descriptions, sitemap, structured data
Google Search Console and Google Analytics connected
Redirects from old pages when redesigning, so you keep your rankings
Training on your CMS and admin panel
get: Analytics you can open any time
need: Access to domain and hosting accounts
A launch date that suits your business

t.purpose: Go live without surprises and leave the client fully in control.
steps: Run the pre-launch checklist
Deploy to production; verify SSL and DNS
Set up 301 redirects (redesigns)
Verify Search Console and submit sitemap.xml
Set up GA4 key events and conversions; Meta Pixel if ads are planned
Move every account into the client's name and email
Record a CMS and admin walkthrough video
Write HANDOVER.md and send the handover email
Book a post-launch check two weeks out
t.exit: Client confirms access to everything and accepts the handover.

c.intro: After launch we help the product earn: automations, AI agents, ads, SEO, and ongoing care.
do: Workflow automations with n8n: leads, emails, reports, follow-ups
WhatsApp agents and broadcasts on the official API (AiSensy)
Website and Telegram chatbots
AI voice agents that answer and make calls
Meta ads for e-commerce and lead generation
Ongoing SEO and content
Maintenance: updates, backups, monitoring and fixes
get: Support channel with agreed response times
need: Feedback on lead and sales quality
Approval for campaigns and new automations

t.purpose: Make the product pay back, and keep it healthy.
steps: Review analytics monthly and write the report
Run Meta campaigns: pixel and Conversions API, audiences, creatives, weekly optimisation
Map manual work and build n8n automations with error alerts
Build WhatsApp flows and templates; get Meta template approval
Build and test voice agents; review call transcripts weekly
Maintenance: dependency updates, backups, uptime monitoring, security patches
Quarterly review with the client: results and next opportunities
t.exit: Ongoing. Each quarter ends with a review and a plan for the next one.

COMPARE: You explain your business again to every freelancer
You explain it once; research is shared by the whole team
Designer and developer work from different ideas
Designs and code come from the same design system
Website, ads and automations are built separately
Every piece is planned to work together

Maintenance and growth support continue after launch

PROMPTS.title: Lead research before a discovery call
PROMPTS.text:
You are a business analyst at a digital product agency. Research this lead before our discovery call.
Business: [name, website, Instagram]
Industry and city: [ ]

Give me:
1) What they sell and to whom
2) How they get customers today
3) 3 visible problems in their website or social presence
4) 3 direct competitors
5) 8 sharp questions for a 30-minute discovery call
6) Which of our services fit (brand, UX, web/SaaS/ERP build, automation, WhatsApp or voice agents, Meta ads, SEO) and why

PROMPTS.title: Discovery call recap and scope
PROMPTS.text:
Here is the transcript of a discovery call: [paste]

Write:
a) A recap email to the client, under 200 words, plain language, confirming goals, problems and next steps
b) An internal summary: goals, users, constraints, timeline, risks, open questions
c) A recommended scope split into Phase 1 (must-have) and later phases, with the deliverables for each

PROMPTS.title: Competitor Analysis page
PROMPTS.text:
Act as a UX and market researcher. Compare [client / product] with these competitors: [names + urls].

Structure the output exactly like this:
1) Competitor overview: one card per competitor with positioning, business model, audience, key numbers, platform or tech
2) Feature comparison matrix: rows = [features that matter for this product], columns = competitors, values ✓ / ✗ / partial, plus fees
3) What each competitor does brilliantly: one idea per competitor to borrow, and why it works
4) High-converting strategies to apply to [client], each with how to implement it
5) The gap [client] should own: one positioning paragraph
6) The three highest-ROI moves for this specific situation

Mark anything you could not verify, and cite sources.

PROMPTS.title: User interview synthesis
PROMPTS.text:
Below are notes from [n] user interviews for [product]: [paste]

Group the findings into themes (affinity mapping). For each theme give: the insight, 2 supporting quotes, how many participants mentioned it, and one "How might we" question.

Then rank the top 5 pain points by frequency and severity.

PROMPTS.title: UX audit of a page or flow
PROMPTS.text:
Audit this as a senior UX designer: [url or screenshots]

Use Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, WCAG 2.2 AA basics (contrast, focus, labels, alt text) and conversion best practice.

Output a table: issue | where | heuristic or UX law broken | severity (1-4) | evidence | recommended fix | effort (S/M/L).
Finish with the 5 quick wins.

PROMPTS.title: User Personas page
PROMPTS.text:
Using this research: [interview notes / survey results / competitor findings], create [3-4] user personas for [product].

For each persona:
- Name and archetype (e.g. "The Hungry Learner"), role, age, city, main device
- 3-4 tags and main traffic source
- Goals (4), pain points (4), online behaviour (4)
- One quote in their own words
- Decision levers ranked by weight (e.g. social proof, price, preview, design), each scored out of 10
- How to attract them on [product]: 5 specific design or copy moves

Base each point on the research and flag anything that is an assumption.

PROMPTS.title: Userflows page
PROMPTS.text:
Map the complete user flow for [product], from first click to repeat purchase.

Organise it in zones: Entry → Browse → [Product page] → Checkout → Delivery → Return.
For each zone list: the screens or system steps, every decision point with both outcomes (e.g. interested / not convinced), failure and exit paths (bounce, payment failed, link expired), and automation steps (webhooks, n8n, emails).
Add the post-purchase loop (review, subscribe, buy again) and any background system (e.g. download protection).

Output: 1) a Mermaid flowchart, 2) a zone-by-zone walkthrough in plain language.

PROMPTS.title: Attraction Strategy page
PROMPTS.text:
Write an attraction strategy for [product] using these personas: [paste].

1) For each website section in order ([hero, social proof, product grid, credibility, preview, urgency + CTA, FAQ, newsletter]): its job, which personas it serves and why, and one line of copy direction
2) Traffic acquisition: for each channel ([Instagram Reels, Google SEO, LinkedIn, newsletter]) the persona it reaches and the exact tactic
3) How the page answers three questions within 8 seconds: What is this? Is it for me? Can I trust it?
4) The trust hierarchy for each persona: what they need first, second and third
5) Key insights, and one tactical move to make now

PROMPTS.title: UX Strategy page
PROMPTS.text:
Create a mobile-first UX strategy for [page / product], based on these personas and this attraction strategy: [paste].

Part 1, Mobile anatomy: the section order at 375px, with one do and one don't for each section.
Part 2, Layout rules: a table of horizontal padding, minimum tap target, CTA height, body and heading font sizes, line height, section gap and sticky bar height; plus a do / don't list.
Part 3, Trust ladder: the trust signals in the order they must appear, and why.
Part 4, CTA strategy: each CTA's position, colour and the persona it targets; expected conversion by scroll depth.
Part 5, Performance UX and typography hierarchy.
End with the 3 rules designers most often break on this kind of page.

PROMPTS.title: Sitemap and MVP scope
PROMPTS.text:
For a [product type] serving these personas: [paste], propose:

1) A sitemap as an indented list, with the purpose of each page
2) The MVP feature list using MoSCoW (must, should, could, won't)
3) What moves to phase 2, and why

PROMPTS.title: Strategy Brief page
PROMPTS.text:
Write a strategy brief for [client] from these research pages: [paste Competitor Analysis, User Personas, Attraction Strategy, UX Strategy]

Sections: business goals and KPIs, audience, problem statement, positioning statement, brand story (how the founder's story reaches the end customer), attraction strategy (how users discover, trust and convert), experience principles, scope and roadmap, risks.

Keep it under 2 pages.

PROMPTS.title: UX Research Presentation
PROMPTS.text:
Turn this research pack into a client presentation: [paste or summarise Competitor Analysis, User Personas, Userflows, Attraction Strategy, UX Strategy, Strategy Brief].

12 slides at most. For each slide: title, 3 bullet points in plain language, and the visual to show (matrix, persona card, flow diagram, mobile anatomy). Open with the client's goal; end with recommendations and the decisions we need from them. Explain any UX term in one line.

PROMPTS.title: Design Inspirations and direction
PROMPTS.text:
Create a design direction brief for [client].
Brand values: [ ]
Audience / personas: [ ]
Competitors: [ ]
References saved on the Design Inspirations page (Refero, Mobbin, Dribbble): [describe]

Give 3 distinct directions. For each: mood keywords, colour palette with roles, type pairing, imagery style, key UI patterns, and one sentence on how it tells the client's story. Recommend one and explain why.

PROMPTS.title: Branding page
PROMPTS.text:
Create a brand system brief for [client], using this strategy brief and these personas: [paste].

Cover all nine parts:
1. Logo system (primary, secondary, icon, usage rules)
2. Colour system (roles and hex values, contrast-checked)
3. Typography (display, body, scale)
4. Visual style
5. Graphic elements
6. Brand voice (tone, do / don't, sample lines)
7. Iconography
8. Layout design (grid, spacing)
9. Mockups to produce
Tie each choice back to the brand story.

PROMPTS.title: Wireframes page
PROMPTS.text:
Write a wireframe spec for the [page name] of [product], following this UX strategy: [paste section order and rules].

For each section in order: purpose, content blocks, real copy direction (no lorem ipsum), primary and secondary actions, mobile vs desktop differences, and states (empty, loading, error). Keep it ready to draw in Figma.

PROMPTS.title: Design system in Storybook
PROMPTS.text:
Read DESIGN.md and the tokens in /design/tokens.json. Set up Storybook for this React project.

Create these components using the tokens only, with no hard-coded colours: [Button, Input, Select, Card, Modal, Table, Badge].
Each component needs: props for variants and sizes, accessible states (focus, disabled, error), and a story file showing every variant with docs.

Do not invent new tokens. Ask me if one is missing.

PROMPTS.title: CLAUDE.md for a new repo
PROMPTS.text:
Create CLAUDE.md for this repo. Include:
- Project summary and who it is for
- Tech stack and versions
- Folder structure
- How to run, test and build
- Coding conventions
- Design system rules: use tokens from DESIGN.md and components from /components/ui
- Security rules: no secrets in code, validate all input, auth check on every protected route
- Definition of done
- Things to never change without asking

PROMPTS.title: Architecture document
PROMPTS.text:
Act as a solutions architect. From this PRD: [paste]

Propose: system architecture (as a Mermaid diagram), tech stack with reasons, data model (tables, key fields, relations), roles and permissions matrix, API endpoints, third-party integrations, hosting and environments, backup and scaling plan, and security risks with mitigations.

Write it as ARCHITECTURE.md.

PROMPTS.title: Pre-launch security review
PROMPTS.text:
Review this codebase for security before launch. Check:
secrets in code or git history, auth and session handling, role checks on every route, input validation and injection, XSS, CSRF, file uploads, rate limiting, CORS, dependency vulnerabilities (npm audit), error messages that leak data, and environment setup.

List findings by severity with file paths and the fix. Do not change code until I approve.

PROMPTS.title: SEO launch pack
PROMPTS.text:
Prepare SEO for the launch of [site]. For each page in this sitemap: [paste]
give: title (max 60 characters), meta description (max 155), H1, primary and secondary keywords, schema type, and internal links.

Also give: a robots.txt, a sitemap.xml checklist, a 301 redirect map from these old URLs: [list], and the Search Console and GA4 setup steps.

PROMPTS.title: Handover email
PROMPTS.text:
Write a project handover email for [client]. Include:
- Live URL and repo link
- Where the admin/CMS login is (not the passwords)
- Every account now in their name: domain, hosting, analytics, Search Console, WhatsApp API, n8n
- Documentation links and the training video link
- Support plan and how to raise an issue
- Our recommended next growth steps

PROMPTS.title: n8n workflow design
PROMPTS.text:
Design an n8n workflow for this manual process: [describe]

Give: the trigger, every node in order (node type, purpose, key settings), data mapping between nodes, error handling and retries, where credentials are stored, a test plan with sample data, and how we will be alerted when it fails.

PROMPTS.title: WhatsApp agent on AiSensy
PROMPTS.text:
Design a WhatsApp agent for [business] on AiSensy.

Output: use cases (FAQ, lead capture, order status, booking), conversation flows with buttons and lists, message templates that need Meta approval (category and text with variables), when to hand over to a human, data to save to the CRM, opt-in wording, and 5 test conversations including edge cases.

PROMPTS.title: AI voice agent script
PROMPTS.text:
Write the system prompt and call script for an AI voice agent for [business].
Direction: [inbound / outbound]. Goal: [book appointment / qualify lead / support].

Include: greeting, disclosure that it is an AI assistant, qualification questions, objection handling, tool calls needed (calendar, CRM), when to transfer to a human, voicemail script, and when to end the call. Keep sentences short for speech.

PROMPTS.title: Meta ads launch plan
PROMPTS.text:
Plan a Meta ads launch for [brand / product].

Give: campaign objective and structure, 3 audience sets (interest, lookalike, retargeting), 5 creative concepts (hook, visual, primary text), landing page checks, pixel and Conversions API events to track, a 30-day test budget split in percentages, and the KPIs to review every week.

RESEARCH.name: Competitor Analysis
RESEARCH.purpose: Where competitors are strong, what to borrow, and the gap the client can own.
RESEARCH.client: Competitors compared feature by feature, what each does best, and the gap you can own.
sections: Competitor overview: positioning, model, audience and key numbers
Feature comparison matrix (✓ / ✗ / partial), including fees
What each competitor does brilliantly: ideas to borrow
High-converting strategies to apply to this project
The gap we should own: one positioning paragraph
RESEARCH.ex: ZebraLearn, Gumroad, Payhip and Podia compared on 10 features, from chapter previews to timed download links and platform fees.

RESEARCH.name: User Personas
RESEARCH.purpose: Who we design for, what moves them to buy, and how to attract each one.
RESEARCH.client: Each customer type with goals, pain points, what makes them buy, and how to attract them.
sections: Name and archetype, role, age, city, main device
One quote in their own words
How to attract this persona: specific design and copy moves
RESEARCH.ex: 4 personas, each tied to a traffic source: Google and YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram Reels, newsletter.

RESEARCH.name: Userflows
RESEARCH.purpose: Every path a visitor can take, from first click to repeat purchase.
RESEARCH.client: Every path your customer can take, including drop-offs, failures and repeat purchases.
sections: Zones in order: entry, browse, product page, checkout, delivery, return
Every decision point with both outcomes
Failure and exit paths: bounce, payment failed, link expired
Post-purchase loop: review, subscribe, buy again
Background systems, such as download protection
RESEARCH.ex: 8 zones from Instagram, Google or referral to download, with Razorpay/Stripe checkout and n8n delivery.

RESEARCH.name: Attraction Strategy
RESEARCH.purpose: What each page section must do, for whom, and which channel brings which persona.
RESEARCH.client: What every section of your site must do, for which customer, and where your traffic comes from.
sections: Each website section: its job, personas served, copy direction
The 8-second rule: What is this? Is it for me? Can I trust it?
Key insights and one tactical move to make now
RESEARCH.ex: 8 landing-page sections mapped to 4 personas; Reels, SEO, LinkedIn and newsletter mapped to who they reach.

RESEARCH.name: UX Strategy
RESEARCH.purpose: The rule system the design must follow, mobile first.
RESEARCH.client: The layout, trust and call-to-action rules your design will follow, mobile first.
sections: Mobile anatomy: section order with a do and don't for each
Layout rules: padding, tap targets, CTA height, type sizes, section gaps
Do and don't list for layout decisions
Trust ladder: the order trust signals appear
CTA positions, colours and conversion by scroll depth
Performance UX: images, fonts, PageSpeed target, checkout
RESEARCH.ex: 375px mobile anatomy, a 7-step trust ladder, and four CTAs, each aimed at a different persona.
